svg.title: Latest phishing pipeline flow - accuracy first lexical-first hashing
svg.desc: Figma-ready SVG showing the latest pipeline flow: holdout input, lexical-first admission, DNS on lexical survivors, staged fetch with fetched_visual_missing support, stage 1 debug artifacts, stage 2 enrichment and model validation, final hybrid classification, and delivery outputs.
svg.text: Current implementation in comparison.py + pipeline.py: lexical gate first, DNS only on survivors, staged fetch, review-only failures, and fetched_visual_missing safe continuation.
Stage 0-1: Input, Lexical Gate, DNS Gate, and Hashing Shortlist
Stage 1 is now intentionally narrow: only lexical survivors are allowed to consume DNS and Playwright capacity.
Rejects go to DNS audit artifacts.
Adaptive downshift enabled, active page floor=8
Goal: stable full HTML capture and lower stage-wide collapse risk, not maximum throughput.
Only lexical survivors consume DNS and browser work. This is the main structural fix for the earlier server overload pattern.
Capture final landing URL + HTML content.
Run parked-page detection before screenshot work.
If screenshot fails but HTML succeeds:
CPU evidence: domain, favicon, SSL, HTML hash, domain hash, keywords
CLIP screenshot similarity runs only if screenshot bytes exist
Admit shortlist rows from fetched states only
Stage 1 result is `holdout.csv` plus review and debug artifacts.
Now shows lexical, DNS, and hash-stage exclusions.
DNS now runs after lexical prefiltering.
Only fetched-like rows survive into holdout.
Failed and timed-out rows stay auditable, but they do not continue into final classification.
`fetched_visual_missing` continues with CPU evidence and reduced visual support.
Stage 2: Validation, Infra Enrichment, and Supporting Models
Only rows with `fetch_status in {fetched, fetched_visual_missing}` are eligible here. Parked and stale failed rows are blocked.
Skip stale failed rows even from reused holdouts.
DNS records, GeoIP, RDAP/WHOIS, hosting IP, ISP, country.
Used as corroboration, not as the only anchor.
Agreement and runtime health logged in debug CSVs.
Feature status, model agreement, final evidence trace.
Final labels are driven by lexical evidence plus corroboration, with safer treatment of missing visual evidence and strict blocking of failed fetches.
`Suspected` = weaker corroboration / suspicious infra / partial support
Only classified eligible rows appear here.
No failed or timed-out row should reach
final output under the current design.
accuracy, stable fetch, and auditable exclusions
Not optimized for maximum browser throughput.
